Technical premium of an excess of loss layer

Source: R/reinsurance_pricing.R
technical_premium.Rd

The premium of a layer from its expected loss: the total premium covers the expected loss and a loading for expenses, brokerage and profit, and with paid reinstatements part of it comes as reinstatement premium, so the upfront premium is lower.

Usage

technical_premium(
  expected_loss,
  limit,
  loading = 0,
  reinstatements = 0,
  reinstatement_rate = 1,
  used = NULL
)

Arguments

expected_loss

The expected loss of the layer.

limit

The limit of the layer.

loading

The share of the total premium for expenses, brokerage and profit, from 0 to below 1. Defaults to 0.

reinstatements

The number of paid reinstatements; 0 (the default) for none, Inf for unlimited.

reinstatement_rate

The rate of each reinstatement, as a share of the upfront premium. Defaults to 1 (100%).

used

The expected reinstated cover as a share of the limit; NULL (the default) for \(\min(EL / l, n)\).

Value

A list with expected_loss, total_premium, upfront_premium, reinstatement_premium (expected), rate_on_line (the upfront premium over the limit), payback (the limit over the upfront premium, in years) and used.

Details

The total premium is \(EL / (1 - loading)\). With \(n\) reinstatements paid at the rate \(r\) of the upfront premium \(P\), pro rata as to amount, the expected reinstatement premium is \(P r u\), where \(u\) is the expected reinstated cover as a share of the limit, \(E[\min(S, n l)] / l\) for the annual layer loss \(S\); so \(P = EL / ((1 - loading)(1 + r u))\). Without used, \(u\) is taken as \(\min(EL / l, n)\), which is exact when the annual losses never exceed the reinstated cover; the burning cost's layer losses at the rating premium give a better one (see the examples). For the reinstatement premiums of each simulated year, see reinstatement_premium.

See also

Other reinsurance pricing functions: burning_cost(), credibility_weight(), mbbefd_curve(), pareto_rating(), property_exposure_rating()

Examples

technical_premium(expected_loss = 1.2e6, limit = 4e6, loading = 0.25,
                  reinstatements = 1, reinstatement_rate = 1)
#> $expected_loss
#> [1] 1200000
#> 
#> $total_premium
#> [1] 1600000
#> 
#> $upfront_premium
#> [1] 1230769
#> 
#> $reinstatement_premium
#> [1] 369230.8
#> 
#> $rate_on_line
#> [1] 0.3076923
#> 
#> $payback
#> [1] 3.25
#> 
#> $used
#> [1] 0.3
#> 

# the reinstated cover used in each past year, at the rating year's premium
bc <- burning_cost(xl_large_losses, xl_premium[, c("year", "premium")], 1e6, 4e6,
                   inflation = 0.04, rating_premium = 60e6)
used <- mean(pmin(bc$by_year$at_rating_premium, 1 * 4e6)) / 4e6
technical_premium(bc$expected_loss, 4e6, loading = 0.25, reinstatements = 1, used = used)
#> $expected_loss
#> [1] 2782345
#> 
#> $total_premium
#> [1] 3709794
#> 
#> $upfront_premium
#> [1] 2494674
#> 
#> $reinstatement_premium
#> [1] 1215120
#> 
#> $rate_on_line
#> [1] 0.6236686
#> 
#> $payback
#> [1] 1.603416
#> 
#> $used
#> [1] 0.4870854
#>
